title: Substring with Concatenation of All Words
statement: You are given a string s of lowercase letters and a non-empty list words in which every entry is a lowercase string of the same length (the same word may appear multiple times in the list). A block match at index i is a substring of s starting at i whose length is len(words) * word_length and which can be split into consecutive word-length chunks that use every entry of words exactly once each, in any order — duplicates in words must appear that many times among the chunks. Return a list of all block-match starting indices in strictly ascending order. Every index from 0 through len(s) - total_length is a candidate, not just multiples of the word length. Return [] when there is no block match (including when s is empty or shorter than the total length).
reference_solution:
def find_concat_starts(s, words):
    from collections import Counter
    word_len = len(words[0])
    total = word_len * len(words)
    need = Counter(words)
    starts = []
    for i in range(len(s) - total + 1):
        chunks = Counter(s[i + k * word_len:i + (k + 1) * word_len] for k in range(len(words)))
        if chunks == need:
            starts.append(i)
    return starts
hints: All words share one length, so any candidate window splits cleanly into fixed-size chunks. What compact summary of a window lets you compare it against the target collection when order is irrelevant but duplicate counts still matter?
Build a Counter of words once. A window starting at i matches iff the Counter of its word-length chunks equals that target Counter — a plain set loses the duplicate counts.

Loop i over every index 0..len(s)-total (not just multiples of word_len). For each i, slice the window into len(words) chunks of word_len, build Counter(chunks), and append i when it equals Counter(words).
